1.1: John the Baptist was out in the wilderness, not the temple. Ain't that just like God? He ain't start this movement in the synagogue but in the sticks.
1.2: John was dripped in camel's hair and locust breath—not exactly IG ready—but his message was fire. "Repent and get ready." No fluff, no filter. Just truth. 🔥
1.3: Folks came from all over to confess, repent, and get dipped in water. John was prepping hearts for the One comin' with real power.
1.4: And John knew his role. He wasn't the main act. He said, "I ain't even worthy to unstrap His sandals." That's humility on 10. ✨
1.9: Jesus showed up and got baptized. Not 'cause He needed to—but to model submission. Soon as He came up out the water? Heaven opened. The Spirit descended. The Father spoke. Whole Trinity stepped on the scene. 🙌
1.12: But right after that high moment? The wilderness. The Spirit sent Jesus out there. Not the devil. The Spirit did. You ever get tested right after a blessing? Yeah, that.
1.13: For 40 days, He was in survival mode—fastin', wild animals, and the enemy throwin' shade. But He ain't fold. He was built for it. 💪🏾
1.14: After John got locked up, Jesus started preachin'. His message? "The Kingdom's here. Time to repent and believe." Straightforward. No gimmicks.
1.16: Then He saw Simon and Andrew. They was workin'. Jesus said, "Follow Me, I'll make y'all fishers of people." And they immediately dropped their nets. No excuses. No hesitation. 🎣
1.19: He pulled up on James and John too—they left their pops in the boat. When Kingdom purpose calls, sometimes you gotta leave comfort and kinfolk behind. 📞
1.21: Jesus pulled up to the synagogue and started teachin'. Not like the usual religious leaders—He had authority. Folks was shook. 👀
1.23: A man with an unclean spirit started wildin' in church. That demon knew exactly who Jesus was: "The Holy One of God."
1.25: Jesus told it to hush and get out. And it did. No long convo. No theatrics. Just power and obedience. Folks ain't never seen nothin' like that. ⚡
1.29: After church, Jesus went to Simon's house. His mother-in-law was sick in bed. Jesus pulled up, took her hand, and lifted her. Fever left. She got up and started servin'. 🏠
1.32: Word spread quick. That night, the whole city showed up at the door. Sick folks. Demon-possessed. Jesus healed everybody. Didn't matter what they came with—He handled it.
1.35: Early the next mornin', Jesus dipped off to a quiet spot to pray. Before He did more miracles, He recharged with the Father. Don't miss that rhythm. Ministry starts in secret. ✨
1.37: The crew came lookin' for Him like, "Everybody's lookin' for You!" But Jesus was like, "Let's go somewhere else. I didn't come just to stay—I came to spread the Word."
1.39: He stayed movin', teachin', and castin' out demons across Galilee.
1.40: A man with leprosy came bold: "If You will, You can make me clean." Jesus was moved with compassion. He touched him. That was major. Leprosy made you untouchable. But not to Jesus. 🖐🏾✨
1.41: He said, "I will. Be clean." And just like that, the man was healed.
1.44: Jesus told him to keep it quiet and go follow the protocol. But the man couldn't hold it in—he spread the news everywhere. And because of it, Jesus couldn't even move around freely no more.

2.1: Jesus came back to Capernaum and word got out quick. The house was so packed folks couldn't even get in the door. But four dudes showed up carryin' their paralyzed friend, and they wasn't leavin' without a miracle.
2.4: The door was blocked? Cool. They climbed the roof. Tore it open. Lowered him down right in front of Jesus. That's bold faith. That's "do whatever it takes" energy. 🧱✊🏾
2.5: Jesus saw their faith—not the man's, their crew's—and said, "Son, your sins are forgiven." That's wild! He came for healing and got forgiveness first.
2.7: The religious leaders got tight: "Who does He think He is? Only God can forgive sins."
2.9: Jesus clapped back, "What's easier—sayin' 'your sins are forgiven' or 'get up and walk'? Just so y'all know I got that authority…" Then He told the man, "Get up, grab your mat, and go home."
2.12: And bruh got up immediately. Whole crowd lost it. They was like, "We ain't never seen anything like this!" 🤯
2.14: Jesus walked by Levi (aka Matthew), a tax collector, and said, "Follow Me." Levi didn't hesitate—he got up and left the bag behind.
2.15: Then Jesus pulled up to Levi's house, chillin' with a whole squad of tax collectors and "sinners." That had the religious folks real uncomfortable. 😒
2.16: They whispered to the disciples like, "Why He eatin' with them?"
2.17: Jesus heard that and said, "Look, healthy folks don't need a doctor—sick ones do. I ain't come to call the righteous, but sinners." Period. That's mission talk. 🩺
2.18: Some folks came askin' why Jesus' disciples ain't fastin' like John's or the Pharisees'.
2.19: Jesus said, "You don't fast while the bridegroom's still here. The time for that's comin'."
2.21: Then He dropped a metaphor: "You can't patch an old cloth with new fabric. And you can't pour new wine into old wineskins—it'll bust."
2.22: Translation? This Kingdom move ain't just a remix. It's a whole new thing. You can't fit this into your old religious system. You gotta stretch. 🍷✨
2.23: One Sabbath, Jesus' crew was walkin' through grainfields, grabbin' heads of grain. The Pharisees got real nitpicky like, "Why they doin' what's unlawful on the Sabbath?"
2.25: Jesus hit 'em with the receipts: "Didn't David eat the priest's bread when he was hungry? Y'all worried about rules, I'm worried about needs."
2.27: Then He said, "The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath." Mic drop.
2.28: And just so we clear, He said, "The Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath." In other words: I run this. 🗣️👑

3.1: Jesus pulled up to the synagogue, and there was a man with a messed-up hand. The Pharisees was already watchin' Him close like, "Let's see if He gon' heal on the Sabbath so we can catch Him slippin'."
3.3: But Jesus wasn't hidin'. He told the man, "Come stand right here in front of everybody." 👀
3.4: Then He asked the haters, "Is it lawful to do good or evil on the Sabbath? Save a life or kill?" They stayed quiet—mouths shut, but hearts loud with hate.
3.5: Jesus got angry and grieved. That combo right there? Righteous fury. Then He told the man, "Stretch out your hand." He did—and boom, healed on the spot. 🖐🏾💥
3.6: Instead of rejoicing, the Pharisees ran off to plot with the Herodians about how to kill Jesus. Yup. They wanted Him gone for doing good.
3.7: Jesus dipped to the lake with His disciples. Huge crowd followed—folks from Galilee, Judea, Idumea, beyond the Jordan… basically, everybody was pullin' up.
3.9: The crowd was so thick Jesus had to have a boat ready just in case He got pressed too hard. People was tryin' to touch Him just to get healed.
3.11: Even the demons couldn't stay quiet. When they saw Him, they'd scream, "You the Son of God!" But Jesus shut them down. It wasn't time for all that exposure yet. 🤫
3.13: Jesus went up on the mountain and called the ones He wanted. They came without hesitation.
3.14: He appointed twelve to roll with Him—to preach, to cast out demons, and to be with Him. Don't miss that: ministry starts with presence before performance. ⛰️✨
3.17: He gave them power and authority. Simon got named Peter (aka "Rock"). James and John? He called them "Sons of Thunder"—Jesus gave nicknames, too. He was personal with it. 🔥
3.19: He built His team with fishermen, a tax man, a zealot, and even Judas, who would eventually betray Him. Still chose him.
3.20: Jesus came home, and the crowd was so wild He couldn't even eat.
3.21: His own family tried to grab Him like, "He out his mind." They didn't get it.
3.22: The scribes from Jerusalem pulled up talkin' wild: "He got a demon. He cast out demons by Beelzebub."
3.23: Jesus shut that foolishness down with bars: "How can Satan cast out Satan? A kingdom divided can't stand. Y'all sound goofy."
3.26: He said, "If Satan fighting himself, he done." And then He hit 'em with truth: "You gotta tie up the strong man before you can rob his house." Jesus was sayin'—I already tied Satan up. That's how I'm out here freeing folks.
3.29: Then He gave 'em that warning: "Every sin can be forgiven… except blaspheming the Holy Spirit." Why? Because they saw real power and called it evil. That's dangerous ground. ⚠️
3.31: Jesus' mama and brothers pulled up and stood outside. Folks told Him, "Your family outside askin' for You."
3.33: Jesus said, "Who's My mother? Who's My brothers?"
3.34: Then He looked around at the people sittin' with Him and said, "Y'all are My family—whoever does God's will."
3.35: That hit hard. Bloodline don't determine closeness—obedience does. That's Kingdom. 👑

4.1: Jesus hopped in a boat to teach, 'cause the crowd was deep on the shoreline. So He gave 'em a parable—a story with spiritual weight tucked in.
4.3: A farmer went out throwin' seeds. Some landed on the path—birds snatched it up. Some hit rocky ground—sprouted fast but had no roots. Some landed in thorns—choked out before it could grow. But some hit good soil—and that seed went crazy: 30, 60, 100 times more.
4.9: Jesus ended with, "If you got ears, use 'em." In other words: don't just hear this—really listen. 👂🏾🌱
4.10: When the crowd left, His crew pulled up like, "Break that story down for us." And Jesus said, "Y'all been given the mystery of the Kingdom—but some folks just hear stories and stay blind to what's real."
4.14: Then He unpacked it: the seed is the Word.
4.15: Path = folks who hear it but Satan snatches it fast.
4.16: Rocky ground = folks who get hyped but fold under pressure.
4.18: Thorny ground = folks too distracted by money, stress, and life drama.
4.20: Good soil = folks who hear it, take it in, and bear fruit. So don't just aim to hear the Word—be good soil. Let it root. Let it grow. Let it multiply. 🌾
4.21: Jesus said, "Nobody lights a lamp just to put it under the bed." Nah. Light gotta shine.
4.22: Everything hidden gon' get exposed. Secrets won't stay buried. And if you lean into this truth, you'll get even more. But if you ignore it? Even what you got will slip away.
4.25: In the Kingdom, how you handle the truth determines what more you get. 📖💡
4.26: Jesus said the Kingdom of God is like a man planting seeds, then goin' to sleep. The seed sprouts and grows—but he don't know how.
4.28: First the blade, then the head, then the full grain. And when it's ripe? He harvests. Translation? God's work grows slow, steady, and invisibly—but it's comin'. You just gotta trust the process. ⏳🌾
4.30: Jesus dropped one more: "What can we compare the Kingdom to? It's like a mustard seed—the tiniest of all."
4.32: But when it grows? It becomes a whole tree with room for birds to chill in its shade. Small beginnings, big impact. Don't sleep on the seed just 'cause it look little. Faith multiplies when watered. 💪🏾🌳
4.35: That evening Jesus said, "Let's cross over to the other side." They dipped in the boat. But a wild storm hit—waves crashin', boat almost takin' in water.
4.38: Meanwhile, Jesus was knocked out on a pillow. Sleepin' through the chaos. 😴⛈️
4.39: The disciples panicked: "Don't You care we 'bout to die?!" Jesus got up, rebuked the wind, told the waves, "Peace. Be still." And just like that—it was calm.
4.40: Then He turned to them like, "Why y'all so scared? Where's your faith?"
4.41: They sat there shook, whisperin', "Who is this Man that even the wind and sea obey Him?"

5.1: Jesus and the crew landed in the region of the Gerasenes, and soon as He stepped out the boat, here come this man—possessed, wild, livin' in the graveyard. Folks tried to chain him up, but he'd break free every time. Screamin' all night, cuttin' himself with stones. This man was tormented. 💀🔗
5.6: But even with all that, when he saw Jesus from a distance, he ran to Him and dropped to his knees. The demons inside him knew exactly who Jesus was: "Son of the Most High God."
5.9: Jesus asked, "What's your name?" The demon said, "Legion… we many." They begged not to be cast out the region, so Jesus let 'em go into some pigs—and the pigs ran off a cliff into the sea. Whole herd drowned.
5.15: Folks came runnin' and saw the same man who used to be wildin'—now clothed, calm, and sittin' with Jesus. That scared them more than the demons did. 👀
5.17: They told Jesus to leave their region. Imagine that: power shows up… and they push it away.
5.18: As Jesus was leavin', the man begged to come with Him. But Jesus said, "Nah—go back home. Tell your people what God did for you." And that man did. Went and told everybody how Jesus came through. 💬🔥
5.21: Jesus crossed back over, and a big crowd met Him. Then Jairus—a synagogue leader—pulled up desperate. His daughter was dyin'. He begged Jesus to come heal her.
5.24: Jesus said "Let's go," but on the way, a woman who'd been bleeding for twelve years showed up. She had spent everything tryin' to get better, but nothing worked.
5.28: She said to herself, "If I just touch His clothes, I'll be healed." And she did it—snuck up and touched His cloak—and instantly, the bleeding stopped. 🙌🏾💫
5.30: Jesus felt that power leave Him. He turned around like, "Who touched Me?" The disciples was like, "Bruh, the crowd pressin' all up on You, how You gon' ask that?"
5.33: But Jesus kept lookin'. The woman came forward, shook and scared, and told Him the truth. And Jesus? He ain't shame her. He said, "Daughter, your faith made you whole. Go in peace, be healed." 💖👑
5.35: While He was still speakin', somebody came from Jairus's house like, "Don't bother Jesus no more—your daughter died."
5.36: But Jesus overheard and said, "Don't be afraid. Just believe." 💭
5.37: He only let Peter, James, and John come with Him. When they got to the house, people was cryin' loud. Jesus was like, "Why y'all cryin'? She not dead—just sleepin'." They laughed at Him.
5.40: He kicked everybody out. Took the girl's parents and His three disciples, went in the room, and took her hand.
5.41: He said, "Talitha koum"—"Little girl, get up." And immediately, she stood up and started walkin'. She was twelve.
5.42: Everybody was stunned. But Jesus told them, "Keep it quiet. And go get her somethin' to eat."

6.1: Jesus rolled back to His hometown with His disciples. When Sabbath hit, He started teachin' at the synagogue, and folks was amazed—but not in a good way.
6.2: They was like, "Ain't this the carpenter? Mary's boy? James, Joses, Judas, and Simon's brother? Don't His sisters still stay 'round here?" Basically, they couldn't see the divine 'cause they was too focused on the domestic. 🙄
6.4: And Jesus said, "A prophet always get love—except in his hometown, with his own folks." Whew.
6.5: He couldn't do many miracles there, 'cause their faith was low. He healed a few sick folks and kept it movin'. Even Jesus was like, "Wow... y'all really don't believe." 😔
6.7: Jesus called the Twelve and sent 'em out two by two. Gave 'em authority over unclean spirits.
6.8: Told 'em, "Don't take nothin' but a staff. No bag, no bread, no coins. Wear sandals, but don't even bring a backup tunic."
6.10: He was teachin' them: Depend on God, not your own supply.
6.11: He said, "If a place don't welcome y'all, shake the dust off your feet as a warning. Keep it pushin'."
6.12: So they went out preachin' repentance, castin' out demons, and anointin' the sick with oil. Kingdom on the move. 🛫🔥
6.14: Word about Jesus was spreadin', and King Herod heard. Some said He was Elijah. Others said He was a prophet. But Herod was like, "That's gotta be John the Baptist—risen from the dead!"
6.17: Flashback: Herod had John locked up 'cause John called him out for marryin' his brother's wife, Herodias. John said, "That ain't right," and Herodias was heated.
6.20: Herod actually liked listenin' to John—but he was too weak to do right. Then came his birthday party...
6.22: Herodias' daughter danced, and Herod got so hyped he made a reckless vow: "Ask anything—I'll give it to you."
6.24: She asked her momma, who said, "Tell him you want John the Baptist's head on a platter." 💀
6.26: Herod was shook but didn't wanna look weak in front of his guests. So he sent the order. John got beheaded in prison.
6.28: The girl brought the head to her momma. John's disciples came later and buried his body. Tragic. A prophet silenced by pride and politics. 📉
6.30: The apostles came back, told Jesus everything they'd done. He said, "Let's rest—y'all need a break." So they dipped to a quiet spot.
6.34: But the crowd beat them there. Jesus saw them and felt compassion. They looked like sheep without a shepherd. So He taught them again.
6.35: It got late. The disciples said, "Send them away to buy food." But Jesus said, "You feed them." 😅
6.37: They was like, "Uhh... that would cost way too much."
6.38: Jesus asked, "What y'all got?" They said, "Five loaves and two fish."
6.39: Jesus told the crowd to sit down in groups. He blessed the food, broke it, gave it to the disciples, and they served everybody.
6.42: Everybody ate till they were full. And they had twelve baskets of leftovers. Oh—and there were over 5,000 men. Not even counting women and kids. 🐟🍞🙌🏾
6.45: Right after that, Jesus told the disciples to get in the boat and go ahead to Bethsaida. He sent the crowd away and went up on the mountain to pray.
6.48: Later that night, the boat was stuck in a storm. Jesus saw them strugglin' and came walkin' on the water—like it was nothin'.
6.49: They saw Him and thought He was a ghost. Screamed. Jesus was like, "Chill. It's Me. Don't be afraid." 🧊🌊
6.51: He got in the boat and the wind stopped. But the disciples were still in shock. They ain't fully get the miracle with the loaves—they still had hard hearts.
6.53: When they got to Gennesaret, folks recognized Jesus immediately.
6.55: People ran and brought the sick from all over. Wherever He went—villages, towns, country—folks laid out the sick, just hopin' to touch even His robe.
6.56: And everyone who touched Him? Got healed. Just like that. 🧎🏾‍♀️🕊️

7.1: The Pharisees and some scribes pulled up from Jerusalem and noticed Jesus' disciples eatin' with "unclean" hands—as in, they didn't do that whole ritual handwash first. And the religious folks was big mad. 😤🧼
7.3: See, they was stuck on traditions—washin' cups, pitchers, and all kinda extra rules—but they missed the point.
7.6: Jesus hit 'em with, "Y'all care more about tradition than God's commandments." And then He brought receipts: "Moses said honor your parents. But y'all say if someone declares their money 'Corban'—a gift to God—they ain't gotta help their folks."
7.13: He said, "Y'all cancel out God's Word to keep your little man-made rules." Jesus wasn't playin'. He basically said, you know church, but you don't know God. 🗣️
7.14: Jesus called the whole crowd and said, "Listen close—what goes into you doesn't defile you. It's what comes out that shows your heart."
7.17: Later, the disciples still didn't get it, so Jesus broke it down: "Food don't make you dirty spiritually—it just pass through."
7.21: "But evil thoughts? Pride, greed, jealousy, slander, sexual sin, murder—all that? That come from inside."
7.23: Moral of the story? You could wash your hands all day, but if your heart ain't clean, you still dirty. 🚫💔
7.24: Jesus dipped to Tyre—Gentile territory—tryin' to lay low. But this woman found Him. Her daughter had a demon, and she was desperate.
7.26: She begged Jesus to heal her daughter. But Jesus said, "Let the children eat first. It ain't right to toss the kids' bread to the dogs."
7.28: Oop. That sounded cold... but the woman didn't flinch. She said, "Even dogs get the crumbs under the table."
7.29: Jesus was like, "Girl... you get it." He said, "Because of what you said, your daughter's healed." 🙏🏾🔥
7.30: She went home and sure enough—her daughter was free. That's faith with persistence and precision.
7.31: Jesus rolled through Decapolis, and some people brought Him a man who was deaf and could barely speak. They begged Jesus to lay hands on him.
7.33: Jesus pulled him aside from the crowd, touched the man's ears, spit, touched his tongue, looked up to heaven and said, "Ephphatha"—means "Be opened."
7.35: Instantly the man could hear and talk clearly. 🙌🏾🦻🏾
7.36: Jesus told them to keep it quiet, but they couldn't. The more He told 'em not to talk, the more they spread it.
7.37: Folks said, "He does everything well. He even makes the deaf hear and the mute speak!" They was shook—in the best way.

8.1: The crowd was with Jesus for three days and ran outta food. He told the disciples, "I feel for them—they been with Me and they hungry. I can't send them away like this." 🥺🍞
8.4: The disciples still confused: "Where we gon' get enough bread out here in the middle of nowhere?"
8.5: Jesus asked, "How many loaves y'all got?" They said, "Seven."
8.6: He told the crowd to sit down. Took the bread, gave thanks, broke it, and had the disciples pass it out. Did the same with a few small fish.
8.8: Everybody ate till they were full—4,000 people—and there were seven baskets of leftovers.
8.10: Then Jesus sent them home and bounced to Dalmanutha. Moral of the story? If He did it before, He'll do it again. Same Jesus, same power. 🍽️
8.11: The Pharisees pulled up tryin' to test Jesus—askin' for a sign from Heaven.
8.12: Jesus sighed deep. Like, real deep. You could hear the frustration. "Why y'all always askin' for a sign? No sign for this generation." And He left them. That's it. Just walked away. ✌🏾
8.13: Some folks don't need more proof—they need more faith.
8.14: In the boat, the disciples realized they forgot to bring bread—only had one loaf with them. And Jesus said, "Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and Herod."
8.16: They started whisperin', "He talkin' about bread 'cause we ain't bring none."
8.17: Jesus overheard and was like, "Y'all serious right now? After all the miracles y'all saw, you still worried about bread?"
8.19: "I fed 5,000—how many baskets did you pick up?" "Twelve." "Fed 4,000—how many baskets?" "Seven."
8.21: "So how y'all still don't get it?" Jesus was tellin' them: this ain't about bread, it's about belief. 🍞👀
8.22: At Bethsaida, some folks brought a blind man and begged Jesus to touch him.
8.23: Jesus led him out the village, spit on his eyes (yes, again), laid hands on him, and asked, "Can you see?"
8.24: The man said, "I see people... but they look like trees walkin'."
8.25: Jesus laid hands on him again—and this time, he saw everything clearly. 🧠👁️💡
8.26: Some healing ain't instant. Sometimes God works in layers. He see the full picture even when your vision's still fuzzy.
8.27: On the way to Caesarea Philippi, Jesus asked His crew, "What's the word in the streets—who do people say I am?"
8.28: They said, "John the Baptist... Elijah... one of the prophets."
8.29: Then He asked, "But who do y'all say I am?"
8.30: Peter spoke up: "You're the Messiah." That part. 🎯
8.31: Jesus started teachin' them that the Son of Man was gonna suffer, be rejected, killed, and then rise after three days.
8.32: Peter pulled Jesus aside and tried to correct Him.
8.33: And Jesus turned around and said, in front of everybody, "Get behind Me, Satan! You not thinkin' God's thoughts—just human ones."
8.34: Jesus called the crowd and the disciples and said, "If you wanna follow Me, deny yourself, pick up your cross, and let's go."
8.35: "If you try to save your life, you gon' lose it. But if you lose it for My sake and the gospel's, you'll find it."
8.36: "What good is it to gain the whole world and lose your soul?"
8.38: "If you ashamed of Me now, I'ma be ashamed of you when I come back in glory." 💯🔥

9.1: Jesus said, "Some of y'all standing right here won't taste death before seeing the Kingdom come in power." And a few days later, He took Peter, James, and John up a high mountain.
9.2: Then boom—transfigured. His clothes turned radiant white, brighter than bleach could ever do. Moses and Elijah pulled up, choppin' it up with Jesus. This was heaven touchin' earth. ☁️🔥
9.5: Peter got nervous and said, "Uh… we should build three shelters for y'all." He was talkin' just to talk.
9.7: Then a cloud surrounded them and the Father spoke: "This is My beloved Son. Listen to Him." That's the only commentary needed. 💬✊🏾
9.8: When they looked again, Moses and Elijah were gone—only Jesus remained. God was sayin': the Law and the Prophets had their time, but now it's Jesus all day.
9.9: On the way down, Jesus said, "Don't tell anyone what you saw till I rise from the dead." They was confused—still tryin' to understand resurrection. 📖
9.14: When they got back to the rest of the disciples, a whole scene was goin' down. The crowd, the scribes, and the disciples were all caught up in an argument.
9.17: Jesus asked what was goin' on. A man said, "I brought my son to Your disciples—he's got a spirit that makes him mute, throws him into seizures, even tries to kill him. But they couldn't cast it out."
9.19: Jesus sighed again: "How long I gotta deal with y'all's lack of faith?" 😤
9.20: He told them to bring the boy. The spirit saw Jesus and acted up—threw the boy down, foam at the mouth.
9.21: Jesus asked the father how long it had been like this. He said, "Since he was a kid. If You can do anything, help us."
9.23: Jesus said, "If I can? All things are possible for the one who believes."
9.24: The father shouted, "I believe! But help my unbelief!" That's real. Faith and doubt can live in the same heart—but one still chooses to reach for Jesus. 🙏🏾💥
9.25: Jesus rebuked the spirit. It came out violently, but the boy was healed. Later, the disciples asked, "Why couldn't we cast it out?"
9.29: Jesus said, "This kind only comes out through prayer." Some battles need deeper focus. Not hype—humility.
9.30: Jesus and His crew passed through Galilee lowkey. He didn't want crowds this time—He wanted to teach.
9.31: He told them again: "The Son of Man gon' be delivered, killed, and rise on the third day."
9.32: But they still ain't get it. And they were too scared to ask. Sometimes we don't ask 'cause we don't want the answer. 👀
9.33: On the way to Capernaum, Jesus asked them, "What y'all was arguin' about back there?"
9.34: They stayed quiet—'cause they had been debating who was the greatest. Oop. 😬
9.35: Jesus sat down and taught them: "If you wanna be first, be last. Be the servant of all."
9.36: Then He brought a child into the middle and said, "Whoever welcomes a child in My name welcomes Me—and not just Me, but the One who sent Me." 👶🏾❤️
9.37: The Kingdom ain't about position—it's about posture.
9.38: John said, "Teacher, we saw someone castin' out demons in Your name, but he ain't one of us, so we told him to stop."
9.39: Jesus said, "Don't stop him. If he ain't against us, he for us."
9.41: "Anyone who gives y'all even a cup of water 'cause you mine? That person won't lose their reward."
9.42: Translation: Don't gatekeep God. If the work is Kingdom, don't kill it just 'cause it didn't come through your circle. 👐🏾🌍
9.43: Jesus said, "If you cause one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it'd be better to tie a millstone 'round your neck and take a swim."
9.45: And He kept goin': "If your hand causes you to sin—cut it off. If your eye causes you to sin—pluck it out."
9.47: Harsh? Yup. But He's showin' how serious sin is. Better to lose a limb and enter life than keep it and end up in destruction. 🛑🔥
9.49: Salt was the final metaphor: "Everyone will be salted with fire." Translation—refinement ain't optional.
9.50: He said, "Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with each other." That's flavor and unity. ✨

10.1: Jesus went to Judea, and the crowds came again. As usual, He taught 'em.
10.2: The Pharisees pulled up tryin' to trap Him: "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?"
10.3: Jesus hit 'em with, "What did Moses say?" They replied, "Moses said we could write a certificate and send her off."
10.5: Jesus said, "That was 'cause y'all hearts were hard. But from the beginning, God made marriage sacred—one flesh, not two." 💍
10.9: Then He dropped the mic: "What God joined, let no one separate."
10.10: Later the disciples asked for clarification, and Jesus doubled down: divorcing and marrying someone else? That's adultery.
10.12: This wasn't about legal loopholes—it was about honor and covenant. God ain't lookin' for convenience—He's after commitment.
10.13: Some folks tried to bring kids to Jesus. The disciples tried to block it, but Jesus got heated.
10.14: He said, "Let the children come! Don't stop 'em. The Kingdom belongs to people like this."
10.15: Then He said, "If you don't receive the Kingdom like a child, you ain't gettin' in at all." 😳
10.16: And then—He hugged them, laid hands, and blessed them. That's Jesus. Present, gentle, powerful. 👶🏾💛
10.17: A man ran up, knelt down, and asked, "Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?"
10.18: Jesus said, "Why you call Me good? Only God is good." Then He recited the commandments.
10.20: The man said, "I've kept all that since I was young."
10.21: Jesus looked at him with love and said, "One thing left—go sell everything, give to the poor, and come follow Me."
10.22: The man's face dropped. He walked away sad—he had too much stuff. 💰😔
10.23: Jesus turned to His crew and said, "It's hard for the rich to enter the Kingdom." The disciples was shook.
10.25: He said, "It's easier for a camel to squeeze through a needle than a rich person to enter God's Kingdom."
10.26: They asked, "Who can be saved then?" Jesus said, "With man, impossible. But with God? All things possible." 🙌🏾
10.28: Peter said, "We left everything for You!" Jesus replied, "You ain't gon' miss out. Whatever you gave up—homes, family, land—you gon' get that back with persecution, and eternal life after that."
10.31: "But the last gon' be first, and the first last." Don't let your status fool you.
10.32: Jesus led them toward Jerusalem, and the disciples were both amazed and afraid. Jesus was walkin' bold.
10.33: He pulled the Twelve aside and told them again: "The Son of Man will be handed over, mocked, spit on, whipped, killed—and three days later, He'll rise."
10.34: He ain't sugarcoatin' it. He wanted them to know: glory don't come without suffering. 🎯
10.35: James and John pulled up with a bold ask: "Can we sit at Your right and left in glory?"
10.38: Jesus said, "Can y'all drink the cup I'm about to drink? Be baptized with My baptism?" They said, "We can." He said, "You will—but the seats? That ain't Mine to give."
10.41: The other disciples heard and got heated. Jesus had to call a huddle: "Y'all see how rulers flex on folks? That's not how we roll."
10.43: "If you wanna be great, be a servant. Wanna be first? Be a slave to all."
10.45: "Even the Son of Man ain't come to be served, but to serve—and give His life as a ransom for many." 🛐🙇🏾‍♂️
10.46: They hit Jericho, and a blind man named Bartimaeus was sittin' on the roadside beggin'.
10.47: When he heard Jesus was passin' by, he shouted: "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"
10.48: Folks tried to shut him up, but he yelled louder. Don't let people's comfort kill your cry. 🗣️🔥
10.49: Jesus stopped and said, "Call him here." The same folks that tried to silence him was now like, "Cheer up! He callin' you."
10.50: Bartimaeus threw off his cloak, jumped up, and ran to Jesus. Jesus asked, "What you want Me to do for you?"
10.51: He said, "Rabbi, I wanna see." And Jesus said, "Go. Your faith made you whole." Immediately, he could see—and followed Jesus down the road. 👁️🚶🏾‍♂️

11.1: Jesus got close to Jerusalem and told two of His disciples, "Go to that village up ahead. You'll find a donkey colt tied up—one nobody's ever ridden. Bring it."
11.3: "If anybody asks why, just say, 'The Lord needs it.'" And just like that—they found it, untied it, explained it, and brought it back. No issues. That's divine alignment. ✨🐐
11.7: They threw their cloaks on the colt and Jesus got on. As He rode, people laid coats and palm branches on the road. The streets turned into a Kingdom parade.
11.9: Folks was shoutin': "Hosanna! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!" They knew what this meant—He was claimin' King status. 👑
11.11: Jesus entered Jerusalem, checked out the temple, then dipped to Bethany with the Twelve. Quiet end to a loud entrance. Strategic. Calculated.
11.12: The next day, Jesus was hungry. He saw a fig tree in the distance, lookin' full—but when He got up on it, no fruit.
11.13: It had leaves, but no figs. And Jesus said, "May no one ever eat from you again." The disciples heard it.
11.14: He wasn't just mad at a tree—He was using it as a metaphor: You can look fruitful and still be empty. 🌿🚫
11.15: Jesus entered the temple and wasn't havin' it. Folks was buyin', sellin', exchangin' money—turnin' a sacred place into a marketplace.
11.16: He flipped tables. Knocked over chairs. Shut it all down. He said, "My house is supposed to be a house of prayer for all nations—but y'all turned it into a den of thieves." Whew. 🗣️🔥
11.18: The chief priests and scribes started plottin' how to kill Him. He was messin' with their money and their power.
11.19: But the crowd was locked in. Jesus had their attention.
11.20: The next morning, they saw the fig tree Jesus cursed—withered from the roots.
11.21: Peter pointed it out, and Jesus said, "Have faith in God."
11.23: Then He dropped a Kingdom key: "Whoever speaks to this mountain, tells it to move, and doesn't doubt—but believes it'll happen? It'll be done."
11.24: "Whatever you ask for in prayer, believe you've received it, and it's yours."
11.25: "And when you pray, forgive anybody you got beef with. So your Father in Heaven can forgive you too." 🏔️🙏🏾❤️
11.26: Faith and forgiveness go hand in hand. You can't move mountains while holdin' grudges.
11.27: Back in the temple, the religious leaders pressed Him: "By what authority are You doin' all this?"
11.29: Jesus hit back with a counter-question: "John's baptism—was it from Heaven or from men?"
11.31: They got stuck. If they say "Heaven," Jesus would say, "Then why didn't y'all believe him?" But if they say "from men," the crowd might turn on them.
11.33: So they played it safe: "We don't know."
Jesus said, "Then I ain't tellin' you where My authority come from either." Savage and strategic. Jesus knew the game. ♟️

12.1: Jesus told a parable: A man planted a vineyard, set it up right—fence, winepress, watchtower—and leased it to farmers before goin' away.
12.2: When harvest came, he sent a servant to collect some fruit. They beat him and sent him away. Sent another—they beat him too. Others? They got beat or killed. No respect. No honor. Just violence. 👊🏾🍇
12.6: Finally, the owner said, "Let me send my son. They'll respect him." But those wicked tenants said, "Here come the heir—let's kill him and take what's his."
12.8: They murdered the son and tossed his body out.
12.9: Jesus asked, "What y'all think the owner gon' do?" He answered it Himself: "He gon' come, destroy those farmers, and give the vineyard to someone else."
12.10: He quoted scripture: "The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone."
12.12: The religious leaders knew He was talkin' about them. They wanted to arrest Him right there—but the crowd was too locked in. So they backed off. For now. 👀
12.13: The Pharisees teamed up with Herodians—enemies joinin' forces—to trap Jesus.
12.14: They hit Him with a setup: "Should we pay taxes to Caesar or not?"
12.15: Jesus peeped the trap and said, "Why y'all testin' Me? Bring Me a coin."
12.16: He asked, "Whose face on this?" They said, "Caesar's."
12.17: Jesus said, "Then give Caesar what's his—and give God what belongs to God." 💰✝️
12.18: The Sadducees came next—they don't believe in resurrection, so they tried to clown with a made-up scenario: "A woman married seven brothers, one after the other, all died. In the resurrection, who she married to?"
12.24: Jesus hit back, "Y'all don't know the Scriptures or God's power."
12.25: "In the resurrection, ain't no marriage like y'all know it. It's a whole new reality."
12.27: And then He said, "Y'all say God is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He ain't the God of the dead, but of the living. Y'all way off." 💯💥
12.28: A teacher of the law overheard all this and asked Jesus, "Which command is the most important?"
12.29: Jesus said, "Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, mind, and strength. And love your neighbor as yourself. Ain't nothin' greater than these."
12.32: The teacher agreed: "That's more valuable than sacrifices." Jesus told him, "You not far from the Kingdom." 🧠❤️
12.34: After that? Nobody dared test Him again. He shut it all down with love.
12.35: Jesus asked them a question now: "How can the Messiah be David's son if David calls Him Lord?"
12.37: It was a mystery only Kingdom eyes could see. He was showin' them: I'm not just descended from David—I existed before him.
The crowd was lovin' it. They stayed locked in. 🧩👑
12.38: Jesus warned: "Watch out for the teachers of the law—they love titles, fancy clothes, front-row seats, and long prayers that sound deep but ain't sayin' nothin'."
12.40: "They rob widows and flex spiritual. They gon' be judged extra hard." 🧥📉
12.41: Jesus sat across from the offering box, watchin' folks give. Rich people dropped big bills—but then a poor widow came and gave two tiny coins.
12.43: Jesus said, "She gave more than all of them. They gave out of surplus—she gave outta sacrifice."
12.44: That's Kingdom math. Heaven don't count what you give—it weighs what you keep. 🪙❤️

13.1: As they were leavin' the temple, one of the disciples was like, "Teacher, look how massive these stones are!"
13.2: Jesus hit him with: "You see all this? Not one stone gon' be left on another. It's all comin' down." 🧱💥
13.3: Later on the Mount of Olives, Peter, James, John, and Andrew pulled Him aside and asked, "When is this gon' happen? What's the sign?"
13.4: Jesus ain't give 'em dates—but He gave 'em game.
13.5: First thing Jesus said: "Watch out. Don't let nobody fool you."
13.6: "Many will come sayin', 'I'm the One.' Don't fall for it."
13.7: "You'll hear about wars, earthquakes, famines—don't panic. It's just the beginning of labor pains."
13.9: Then He told 'em: "You gon' get arrested, beaten, dragged into courtrooms—for My name."
13.10: "But that's your chance to testify. The gospel gotta be preached everywhere."
13.11: "Don't stress about what to say—Holy Spirit gon' give you the words."
13.13: "Families gon' turn on each other. You might be hated—but if you hold on to the end, you'll be saved." 🗣️⛓️🔥
13.14: Jesus referenced the "abomination of desolation"—from Daniel's prophecies. He said when you see it standing where it shouldn't be—don't hesitate.
13.15: "If you in Judea, flee to the mountains. Don't go back for nothin'—not your coat, not your stuff."
13.19: "Those days will be the worst the world has ever seen."
13.20: "But God shortened that time—for the sake of the elect."
13.21: And again He said: "If somebody tells you, 'Here's the Messiah!' or 'Look, He's over there!'—don't believe 'em."
13.22: False messiahs and false prophets gon' be out here performin' fake miracles, tryna fool even the chosen. But Jesus said, "I told y'all ahead of time." 👀🚨
13.24: "After all that tribulation, the sun will go dark. The moon won't shine. Stars will fall. Heaven's powers gon' shake."
13.26: "Then they gon' see the Son of Man comin' in the clouds with power and glory." ☁️👑⚡
13.27: "And He'll send angels to gather His chosen ones—from every direction, every corner of earth and heaven."
13.28: Jesus said, "When the fig tree starts sproutin' leaves, you know summer close. Same thing here—when you see these signs, know it's near."
13.30: "This generation won't pass before these things happen."
13.31: "Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words won't." 📜
13.32: "Nobody knows the day or hour—not angels, not even the Son—only the Father."
13.34: Then He told a parable: A man leaves his house and puts his servants in charge. The doorkeeper's job? Stay alert.
13.35: Jesus said, "You don't know when I'm comin' back—could be evening, midnight, dawn. Don't let Me catch you sleepin'."
13.37: Final line: "What I say to you, I say to everyone: Watch." 🕰️👁️

14.1: Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread were two days away. The religious leaders? Already plottin'. They said, "Let's not arrest Him during the festival or the people might riot."
14.2: They feared the crowd more than they feared God. It wasn't about justice—it was about control. 🧠🕵🏾
14.3: Jesus was at Simon the leper's house in Bethany. A woman rolled up with an expensive alabaster jar full of spikenard oil—pure luxury.
14.4: She didn't ask, she didn't wait—she broke the jar and poured it all on His head. That's devotion with no refund policy. 💎💧
14.5: Folks in the room got tight: "Why waste this? We coulda sold it and given to the poor!" But they ain't get it.
14.6: Jesus checked 'em: "Leave her alone. She did something beautiful for Me. You always got the poor—but you won't always have Me."
14.8: "She anointed Me beforehand for burial." And He said, "Wherever the gospel is preached, her story gon' be told."
14.9: She saw what even the disciples didn't. While they were trippin' on budgets, she was tuned into purpose. 🎯
14.10: Right after that, Judas Iscariot went to the chief priests to betray Jesus. They were glad and promised him money.
14.11: That's wild. She gave everything to honor Him. Judas took money to hand Him over. Two hearts, two altars. 💔💰
14.12: On the first day of Unleavened Bread, Jesus told two disciples, "Go find the man carryin' water—follow him. Ask the owner of the house where the guest room is for Me and My disciples."
14.16: They found it just like He said. Already prepared. God don't miss.
14.18: That evening, while they were eatin', Jesus said, "One of y'all gon' betray Me."
14.19: The room got heavy. One by one they asked, "Is it me?" Even Judas kept up the act.
14.20: Jesus said, "The one who dips with Me in the bowl." And then He added, "The Son of Man gon' do what's written—but woe to the one who betrays Him. It'd be better if he was never born." 😞🍷
14.22: Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them: "Take this—it's My body."
14.23: Then He took the cup, gave thanks, passed it around: "This is My blood of the new covenant—poured out for many."
14.25: "I won't drink from the vine again till I drink it new in the Kingdom." He knew what was next. They still didn't. 🥖🍷
14.26: After they sang a hymn, they headed to the Mount of Olives.
14.27: Jesus said, "Y'all gon' scatter. It's written: 'Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will scatter.' But after I rise, I'll meet y'all in Galilee."
14.29: Peter said, "Even if everyone else falls off, I won't."
14.30: Jesus looked at him like, "Before the rooster crows twice, you'll deny Me three times."
14.31: Peter doubled down, "Even if I gotta die with You, I'll never deny You." And all the others said the same.
14.32: Talk is easy when it's safe. But the storm was comin'. 🐓⏳
14.33: They went to Gethsemane. Jesus told His crew, "Sit here while I pray."
14.34: He took Peter, James, and John deeper into the garden. Started feelin' crushed, overwhelmed. "My soul is sorrowful to the point of death."
14.35: He went a little farther, fell down, and prayed: "Abba, Father… if it's possible, take this cup. But not what I want—what You want."
14.37: Came back, found them sleepin'. "Peter, couldn't you watch for one hour? Watch and pray. The spirit willing, but the flesh weak." 😓
14.39: He prayed again. Came back—they were sleepin' again. Same thing the third time. Then He said, "It's time. My betrayer's here."
14.43: While He was speakin', Judas showed up with a mob—swords, clubs, temple guards.
14.45: Judas walked up and gave Jesus a kiss. That was the signal. He betrayed the Savior with a kiss. 🥀💋
14.47: They seized Jesus. One of His disciples (John says it was Peter) pulled out a sword and cut off a servant's ear.
14.48: Jesus said, "Am I a criminal? Y'all rollin' up like I'm dangerous. I was in the temple every day, and y'all ain't touch Me. But this is fulfillin' scripture."
14.50: The disciples ran. All of them.
14.51: A young man (some think Mark himself) tried to follow. They grabbed him—he ran off naked. Left everything. Even his clothes.
14.53: Jesus was brought to the high priest. Peter followed at a distance.
14.55: The chief priests and Sanhedrin looked for fake evidence to justify killin' Him. Testimonies didn't line up.
14.61: Then the high priest asked, "Are You the Messiah, the Son of the Blessed?"
14.62: Jesus said, "I AM. And you'll see the Son of Man sittin' at God's right hand, comin' on the clouds."
14.63: The high priest tore his robes. "Blasphemy! We don't need more witnesses!"
14.65: They condemned Him to death. Then came the spit, the punches, the mocking: "Prophesy, Prophet!"
14.66: While Jesus was bein' mocked inside, Peter was outside, sittin' by the fire.
14.67: A servant girl said, "You were with Jesus." He said, "Nah, I don't know what you talkin' about."
14.69: She told others: "He's one of them." He denied again.
14.70: Later, folks said, "You gotta be one—your accent exposes you." Peter cursed and said, "I don't know that Man!"
14.72: The rooster crowed. A second time. And Peter remembered Jesus' words. He broke down and wept.

15.1: Early in the morning, the chief priests, elders, and scribes made their final move—they bound Jesus and sent Him to Pilate.
15.2: Pilate asked, "Are You the King of the Jews?" Jesus calmly said, "You said it."
15.3: The leaders kept hurlin' accusations, but Jesus stayed silent. Pilate was shook—he had never seen somebody this composed with death knockin'.
15.4: Silence was strength. Jesus didn't need to defend what Heaven had already confirmed. 🤐👑
15.6: Every Passover, Pilate would release a prisoner. This time, the crowd asked for Barabbas—a rebel and murderer.
15.9: Pilate said, "Y'all want me to release Jesus, the King of the Jews?" He knew the leaders handed Jesus over outta jealousy.
15.11: But the priests stirred the crowd up to ask for Barabbas instead. Pilate asked, "Then what should I do with Jesus?"
15.14: Pilate asked, "Why? What did He do?" But they kept shoutin' louder: "CRUCIFY HIM!"
15.15: So Pilate, tryna please the crowd, gave them what they wanted. He released Barabbas, had Jesus whipped, and handed Him over to be crucified. The same crowd that yelled "Hosanna!" was now yelling "Crucify!" Crowds change quick. Be rooted in God, not applause. 📉📢
15.16: The soldiers dragged Jesus inside and called the whole squad. They threw a purple robe on Him and twisted a crown of thorns on His head.
15.18: They mocked: "Hail, King of the Jews!" Then they hit Him with a stick, spit on Him, and fake-worshiped by bowing.
15.20: When they got tired of clownin', they ripped the robe off, put His clothes back on, and led Him to be crucified. The King was humiliated—but He never let go of His mission. Real kings don't prove power—they carry purpose. 👑🌹
15.21: They forced a man named Simon of Cyrene to carry Jesus' cross. He was just passin' by—but got caught up in the story of salvation. 🛑✝️
15.22: They brought Jesus to Golgotha—"Place of the Skull." They tried to give Him wine mixed with myrrh to ease the pain, but He refused. He chose to feel all of it.
15.24: They crucified Him. Stripped Him. Divided His clothes by casting lots.
15.26: The sign above read: THE KING OF THE JEWS—they meant it as mockery, but it was truth. 👑
15.27: Two criminals were crucified next to Him. Passersby mocked: "You said you'd destroy the temple and rebuild it—save yourself!"
15.31: Even the chief priests joined in: "He saved others, but He can't save Himself." They missed it—He could've saved Himself… but then He couldn't have saved us. 🙌🏾❤️
15.33: At noon, darkness covered the land for three hours.
15.34: Then Jesus cried out with a loud voice: "Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?"—"My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?"
15.35: Some thought He was callin' Elijah. Someone gave Him sour wine on a sponge, sayin' "Let's see if Elijah helps Him."
15.37: Then Jesus cried out and took His last breath.
15.38: In that moment, the temple veil tore from top to bottom. Heaven opened what religion tried to keep closed. 🕊️💔⛓️
15.39: The Roman centurion, standin' in front of Jesus, said, "Truly this Man was the Son of God."
15.40: Some women watched from a distance—Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, Salome. They'd followed and served Him faithfully.
15.41: When others scattered, the women stayed. Loyalty don't run when the light fades. ✨
15.42: Evening came. It was Preparation Day before the Sabbath.
15.43: Joseph of Arimathea—a respected council member who believed in the Kingdom—went bold and asked Pilate for Jesus' body.
15.44: Pilate was surprised He was already dead. After confirming with the centurion, he gave the body to Joseph.
15.46: Joseph wrapped Jesus in linen and laid Him in a tomb cut from rock. Rolled a stone in front. Mary Magdalene and Mary of Joses saw where He was laid.
15.47: It looked like the end… but Heaven was just settin' up the next chapter. 🔒🌑

16.1: When the Sabbath passed, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices to anoint Jesus' body. They were ready to honor Him, even in grief.
16.3: Early that Sunday, right as the sun came up, they headed to the tomb. On the way, they wondered, "Who gon' roll that heavy stone away for us?" 🪨😟
16.4: But when they got there—the stone was already rolled back. They stepped in and saw a young man in a white robe chillin' on the right. And they were shook.
16.6: He said, "Don't be scared. You lookin' for Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified. He is risen! He ain't here. Look where they laid Him."
16.7: "Now go tell His disciples and Peter that He's goin' ahead to Galilee. Y'all gon' see Him, just like He said."
16.8: They ran out the tomb trembling, overwhelmed—and they didn't say a word at first, 'cause fear had them frozen. But the tomb was already empty. The silence wouldn't last. 🌅✝️💨
16.9: Jesus appeared first to Mary Magdalene—outta whom He had cast seven demons. That's real love: He trusted the freed to be the first to proclaim.
16.11: She ran to tell the others—who were still grieving. But they didn't believe her. They couldn't wrap their mind around resurrection. 🤯🧎🏾‍♀️
16.12: Later, He appeared in a different form to two of His followers walkin' in the countryside (Luke tells us this was the Emmaus Road moment).
16.13: They went back and told the rest too—but they still didn't believe them either. Even eyewitness accounts won't convince a heart that ain't ready.
16.14: Jesus appeared to the Eleven while they were eatin'. He didn't sugarcoat it—He rebuked them for their unbelief and hard hearts. They didn't believe those who saw Him after He rose.
16.15: Then He commissioned them: "Go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature."
16.16: "Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved. Whoever doesn't believe will be condemned."
16.17: And then He gave them receipts—signs that would follow those who believe: Cast out demons in My name, Speak new tongues, Pick up snakes (unharmed), Drink poison (won't kill them), Lay hands on the sick—they'll recover 👐🏾🔥
16.18: Translation: This ain't a quiet faith. This is power with purpose.
16.19: After all that, Jesus was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.
16.20: The disciples? They went everywhere preachin'—and Jesus was right there with them, showin' up through signs that confirmed the Word. The tomb was the end of death's hold, not the end of the story. Jesus rose, and the movement was just gettin' started. 🚀👑🌍
